**Ranking and probability accuracy answer different questions.** AUC asks whether positives tend to score above negatives. Calibration asks whether cases predicted at 10% actually succeed about 10% of the time. If a probability enters expected revenue, budget planning, or a threshold, its numerical scale matters. [1](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/calibration.html)

But the question overstates the contrast: organic ranking can also combine probabilities with value weights or thresholds, so correct order alone is not always sufficient there. Conversely, a common positive rescaling can leave a particular auction's allocation unchanged.

**Work through a quality-adjusted CPC GSP example.** Let A bid 2 with predicted CTR 0.10, giving score 0.20. B bids 3 with CTR 0.05, giving score 0.15. A wins, and a simplified next-score-over-own-CTR price is 0.15/0.10=1.5 per click. Double both CTRs: scores become 0.40 and 0.30, and the price is 0.30/0.20=1.5 again.

That cancellation can fail with reserves, clipping, heterogeneous distortions, or other payment rules. VCG analysis must specify welfare units and how probabilities enter externality payments. Calibration remains important for interpretable expected outcomes, but “doubling every probability doubles every price” is false in general. Audit calibration by campaign and time, then analyze the exact allocation and payment equations.

**Technical details and references.**

Probability accuracy matters when scores enter expected-value bids, budgets, or thresholds. AUC captures ordering only and cannot detect a uniform probability distortion. Organic ranking also often uses probability values for multi-objective scoring and thresholds, so AUC alone is not generally sufficient there either. [1](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/calibration.html)

If every predicted CTR is multiplied by the same positive constant, pure bid×CTR ordering is unchanged. In a quality-adjusted CPC GSP price that divides the next score by the winner's CTR, that common factor may cancel. Reserves, clipping, budgets, heterogeneous scaling, or other pricing rules can prevent cancellation. VCG effects depend on how modeled welfare and payments are defined.

Therefore doubling probabilities does not universally double prices. Work through the exact mechanism and units, while monitoring calibration by campaign, slice, and time.
